title: When the heart is true
hookLine: truth is known when the heart is true and falsehood's dirt is washed (Asa di Var, ang 468)

lines: A FRIEND BEING STRAIGHT WITH YOU.
WHEN DOES A PERSON KNOW IT?
cards: A friend who's being straight with you shows it, and not only in the words. The eyes stay on yours, the shoulders aren't braced, there's no little gap between what's said and what's meant.
The opposite shows too, even when every word is technically accurate. Truth isn't only a property of sentences. It's a property of people.
Guru Nanak's salok right after the list of koorh doesn't ask what is true. It asks something harder: when can a person be said to know truth at all?

teach.b: The salok on ang 468 is built like a ladder, each rung starting the same way: sach taa par jaaneeai. Truth is known only when. Then Guru Nanak fills in the rest.
Truth is known when the heart itself is true. When the dirt of falsehood comes off, and the body is washed clean.
Truth is known when a person loves truth, when hearing the Name the mind delights, and so finds the door of freedom.

teach.h: THE BODY A FIELD, THE SEED PLANTED.
teach.b: Truth is known when a person knows the way to live: making the body a field and planting the Creator's seed in it.
Truth is known when a person takes true teaching, shows kindness to living beings, and gives what they can.
Truth is known when a person makes their own self the place of pilgrimage, and settles there, guided by the True Guru.
And the last rung: truth is the medicine for everyone. It washes out wrongdoing. Look at what this list is made of.
Not one rung is about winning an argument or holding the right opinion. Every rung is about a person: what the heart loves, how the life is lived, how the hands treat other beings.
In Gurbani, sach is both a name for the One and the quality of a life lined up with the One.
So a true heart isn't one that never makes mistakes. It's a heart with no gap between what it shows and what it is. Yesterday's salok said koorh drowns boatloads.
Today's says truth heals everyone. The washing comes first, and it's daily work.

how: Sikhs hear this salok of truth in the dawn singing of Asa di Var, and Sikhs often recall Guru Nanak's line in Sri Rag that truth stands above all, and truthful living higher still.

an opinion that wins an argument

games.q: you want to know truth. according to Guru Nanak's salok, where does it start?
o: in a heart that is itself true, washed of falsehood.
in a long journey to a holy place.
games.why: truth is known only when the heart is true and the dirt of falsehood is washed off. the self becomes the place of pilgrimage.

practice: Look gently for one small gap between what you show and what is: a white lie you've repeated, a version of yourself you've been performing. Pick just one and picture washing it, the way you'd wash dirt off your hands.

wordCard.voice: Sach, truth: Guru Nanak's ladder says sach is known only when the heart is true, falsehood's dirt is washed, and the life is lived in kindness.
